findings.title: Salesforce service uses prisma without importing it
findings.body: This code calls prisma.credential.update, but the file's imports do not include prisma. This is a TypeScript/ runtime ReferenceError, so Salesforce client construction fails when it reaches the credential update and the Salesforce integration cannot be used.

findings.title: Refreshed Salesforce access token is persisted but not used
findings.body: getClient unconditionally refreshes the token on every construction, parses and stores the refreshed token, but then creates the jsforce Connection with credentialKey.access_token, the old and potentially expired token. API calls made through this connection therefore still fail authentication even though a valid token was just obtained.

findings.title: Google credential is stored as a Zod SafeParse wrapper object
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the Zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), whereas the previous googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the credential object itself. The result is assigned to key and persisted to the credential. On the next use, googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) cannot find the expected top-level token fields, corrupting the Google credential after its first refresh regardless of whether credential sharing is enabled.

findings.title: Minimum token schema strips expiry and replaces the real refresh token with a placeholder
findings.body: The computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] do not create the intended dynamic fields, and Zod strips unknown keys by default, so in sharing mode only access_token survives. Lines 25-27 then set refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token". Callers such as Zoom and Office365 consequently lose expires_in/expiry information (producing NaN or stale expiry) and persist the dummy refresh token over the real one, breaking subsequent refreshes.

findings.title: Sync-mode return value is incompatible with most refresh callers
findings.body: When sharing is enabled this returns the raw fetch Response without checking response.ok or parsing JSON, while the fallback returns whatever each provider-specific refresh function returns. HubSpot expects token fields such as accessToken/expiresIn, Zoho apps expect an Axios response with .data, and Google expects a response with .data; a fetch Response provides none of these. Those integrations will throw, use undefined tokens, or persist an invalid credential object in sync mode.

findings.title: Credential-sync request is sent without any authentication
findings.body: The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT contains only calcomUserId and appSlug, with no shared-secret header, signature, or other credential the parent application can use to authenticate Cal.com. An endpoint implemented to this contract cannot distinguish legitimate Cal.com requests from arbitrary callers who enumerate user IDs to elicit third-party access tokens.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin passes credentialId where refreshOAuthTokens expects userId
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens treats its third argument as the Cal.com user ID and sends it as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint. This call passes credentialId instead of credential.userId. Credential and user IDs are unrelated, so in sync mode the parent application will look up the wrong user or fail to find one and return the wrong/no tokens.

findings.title: Webhook handler has no error handling for malformed or undecryptable payloads
findings.body: The Zod parse at line 31 and the symmetricDecrypt/JSON.parse at lines 57-59 are not wrapped in error handling, and the handler does not restrict the HTTP method. A malformed body, invalid ciphertext, or non-JSON decrypted value throws an unhandled exception and produces a 500 rather than a controlled 400 response, making integration failures indistinguishable from server faults.

findings.title: New credential webhook and token-refresh branching have no tests
findings.body: This PR adds an authenticated credential create/update webhook, AES decryption, a new token-response parser, and sync-mode branches across many calendar/video services, but adds no tests for valid/invalid webhook secrets, decryption failures, create versus update, or sharing-enabled versus disabled refresh behavior. Several of the shipped paths change return shapes and persisted credential formats, and there is no regression coverage to catch that corruption.
